rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and predictions before data, synthetic validation (F/A/Z scenarios, 600 replicates), 4 replication kickoffs (G39, G40, G41, G51), 2 natives (G44 rooms; G51 newcomers + NE38), per-period estimates, confirm.py frozen (NE20 DiD, transfer #45-#47), not run.
rationale.faithfulness: The speed-limit framing holds trivially (counting identity) and its field-limited predictions failed in 3/4 periods: re-allocation is an instant freeze onto named targets (S 1.0-1.4), which the rival R2 predicted. The G44 room contrast (x5.7 at equal switch rate) supports field-set settling, and the slack cleanly separates freeze from churn. Cadence elasticity not identifiable. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A simple kickoff design rule an operator can apply: name the artifact in the goal text and the swarm re-points within 15-30 active min with one switch per agent; free-choice goals take 4-10 h with 5-15 switches per net move. Evidence base is small (4 kickoffs + 1 room contrast with 4 agents); the cadence lever is untested.

one_line: A kickoff that names its target re-allocates the swarm at the Wasserstein speed limit (slack 1.0-1.4, within 0.5 active h); free-choice goals settle 5-40x slower through churn at the same switch rate. The bound itself is a counting identity; cadence effects untested (NE20 held out).
